# Store operations as Phrase steps, not native code

- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; the first vocabulary the prototype needs)
- **Milestone:** Usable v1 (shortest path to a real prototype)
- **Source:** Review of card 135 (Decider D98, 2026-10-28): the Tasks demo app meets the card in structure (five endpoints, eleven specs, zero warnings, all specs pass) but every piece of behaviour sits in five native csharp blocks and the list endpoint carries a fake available input only to have a failure spec. These thin cards close the real gaps so the prototype shows Phrase expressing logic. They sit after the Usable v1 acceptance (138) and before the ZOMBIES card (134).
- **Depends on:** 135
- **Story:** As Ari, I want to find, save, list and remove stored items with Phrase steps, so that my phrases say what happens instead of hiding it in native C#.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a phrase that finds a task by id through TaskStore, When it is written with a Phrase step (no native block) and its spec runs, Then the stored task is returned and an unknown id fails with the declared NotFound, in the same generated shape as today
  2. Given the same for save, list and remove, When the Tasks app is changed to use those steps in its find, create, list, complete and delete phrases, Then its native block count drops by the number of phrases converted, all eleven generated specs still pass and the build has zero warnings
  3. Given the provisional {Record}Store convention, When the steps are added, Then they are a documented language decision (the grammar or the data extension note in the ADR names them) and the card lists every use
